title: Priority Resonance Matrix and Intervention Scheduler
creator: Elena Morris
description:
Summary: Build a scoring and orchestration system (Priority Resonance Matrix) that normalizes disparate customer signals into a single priority score for top accounts, and an Intervention Scheduler that maps scores to prescriptive operational playbooks. Goal is to reduce late-stage escalations and make roadmap intake deterministic for enterprise accounts.

Why: We frequently surface high-touch asks from accounts with noisy signals (support tickets, exec requests, usage anomalies). Current manual triage causes inconsistent commitments and reactive firefighting. A normalized score and systematic intervention schedule lets PM/SE/CS teams coordinate faster, align product commitments, and surface escalation risk into planning.

Signals considered: revenue band, contract renewal window, recent SLA violations, error-rate spikes (from Console), frequency of product/feature requests, customer-sentiment tags from Support, inbound exec escalations, legal/compliance flags, closed-lost deals referencing requested features.

Approach: Phase 1 (MVP, 6 weeks): implement a rules-based normalization layer and a simple linear scoring model with configurable weights. Persist scores in a lightweight priority table and expose via API and a Console list view. Phase 2 (8 weeks): add machine-learned weighting recommendations (offline job), confidence bands, and a scheduler that turns score thresholds into timeboxed interventions (AM outreach, canary rollout, dedicated QE run). Phase 3 (Q2): integrate with Sales CRM to auto-create cases, enable automated runbook triggers for urgent SLO regressions, and enable two-way feedback for score adjustments.

Trade-offs considered: Rules-based MVP gives auditable behavior and faster adoption vs. ML model that needs training data and can be brittle. We favor an explainable scoring model initially and ship ML recommendations as advisory signals. We also decouple score storage from core product DB to avoid heavy coupling with runtime services.

Integration points: Console (list view + dashboard), Alerts (PagerDuty + internal Slack channel), CRM (SFDC/HubSpot webhook), Support (Zendesk tags), Observability (SLO dashboards), and Roadmap intake form (redirect high-score requests into escalation flow).

Deliverables:
- Priority Resonance Matrix service + API (score, contributing signals, score history)
- Intervention Scheduler (rules, calendar, notifications)
- Console list view and a ‘Top Escalations’ dashboard
- Acceptance tests, runbooks and playbook templates for each intervention type

Success criteria (OKR linked):
- O1: Reduce unplanned customer escalations that require roadmap rework by 35% in Q2.
- O2: Increase on-time response to top-account escalations from 48h -> 12h.
- O3: Enable product-led decisions on 80% of top-account intake (vs ad-hoc exec calls).
acceptance_criteria: Priority API returns score and contributor list for any account ID within 200ms
Console shows Top Escalations list with sortable score and last-updated timestamp
Intervention Scheduler can trigger a playbook (AM outreach or canary access) and log the action to the ticket
At least 10 pilot accounts enrolled and tracked for 4 weeks
Automated tests validate score recalculation when new signals arrive (SLO breach, contract update, ticket severity)
metrics: Number of escalations reclassified as actionable vs noise per week
Mean time to first intervention for high-score accounts
Percent reduction in roadmap scope churn due to late escalations
Adoption: percent of CSMs/AMs using the scheduler workflow for escalations
rollout_plan: Week 0-6: internal alpha with 3 enterprise accounts; collect feedback from AM/CS/PM. Week 7-14: expanded beta to 10 accounts, connect CRM webhooks and Console. Week 15-20: cross-functional training and soft-launch for all enterprise AMs, lock-in default weights and runbook templates. Post-launch: weekly retro and Q2 retrospective to evaluate ML weighting pilot.
